reviewer: One project agent reviewed the original English and corresponding publisher formulas for all 12 selected stories before student optimization or either held evaluation.
interpretation: The primary retains every original label and every request. A secondary comparison uses the seven stories without a flagged English/formula discrepancy. Flags apply to entire stories so that different hypotheses from the same source stay together.

flagged.Record 625961af: The original restricts the monkey-or-bird classification to animals. The formula applies it to every entity. The English uses 'a fly' as a noun where the formula uses the predicate for flying.
flagged.Record a2817d1b: The sentence about John having a child denies traveling to Paris and denies having a wedding. The formula denies their conjunction. The concluding July-or-Paris premise also makes exclusive disjunction explicit only in the formal representation.
flagged.Record a403763d: The English denies being picky and needing tuition money. The formula negates a disjunction containing NotPicky, reversing the polarity of the first description. An English 'or, if she is, then' conclusion is represented by exclusive disjunction.
flagged.Record c907fd11: The last premise says that any city in Butte is not in Pierre. The formal variables express that no place containing Butte contains Pierre, reversing the direction of the geographical relation.
flagged.Record ea85a6ba: The sixth premise uses 'and' where the formalization uses disjunction. The final conditional mentioning mild flu and Cholangiocarcinoma also has different conjunction and negation scope.
